content: The CDC’s Colorectal Cancer Control Program (CRCCP) is designed to increase colorectal cancer screening rates, ultimately aiming to save lives. The program collaborates with clinics, hospitals, and other healthcare organizations to enhance access to and participation in colorectal cancer screening. As of January 2024, the CRCCP includes 35 award recipients who are actively working to implement innovative strategies to improve screening rates. In Florida, new approaches such as directly contacting patients and addressing barriers to care have led to significant increases in colorectal cancer screening rates. Rigorous evaluations of the CRCCP have yielded key findings, which are documented in various publications to guide future efforts. The program has also developed a Field Guide for Assessing Readiness to Implement Evidence-Based Cancer Screening Interventions, which assists organizations in determining whether clinics are prepared to adopt and implement cancer screening interventions effectively.
